acceptance.assertion: A real implementor-role native session obtains focused implementation/interface/test excerpts through the same Repomix-backed index/evidence service used by Architect, without a second cache or full-pack injection. Fixture and native checks prove correct path/line/hash/task/workspace provenance, bounded output and explicit partial coverage. An unchanged authorized same-workspace consumer reuses indexed content after its own read checks; a foreign consumer, revoked permission, mismatched implementation worktree or source edit yields denial/stale/refreshed identity, not blindly reused context. Retain the actual request/result and context manifest with source refs.

Use a fixture whose permitted writeScope is src/feature.ts while required interfaces/tests lie elsewhere. The implementor can retrieve those permitted out-of-write-scope reads, and a host read denial still blocks a different file. Packet metadata retains exact write scope and does not add read files to it. No test or documentation treats obtaining context as authorizing broader writes or accepting an artifact; runtime scope/verification/acceptance ownership is explicit. Cross-worktree identity and Architect receipt-parent binding remain intact.

Register/replay the implementor profile without copying the Architect/researcher deny-all rules, hard-coding a model or replacing host tool selection. In a native isolated fixture where normal user/project policy permits them, implementor editing, shell and Code Mode execute harmless test operations and available native LSP/diagnostic access is demonstrated. A separate user/project deny still denies the corresponding implementor operation; no blanket allow overrides it. Architect/investigator/researcher remain narrowly permissioned. Record actual native tool identities and any genuine LSP availability gap; absent host LSP is an explicit unresolved capability, not an invented plugin API or reason to disable normal tools.

Native effective-policy tests attempt implementation-role subagent launch directly and through Code Mode, lazers_research, and any exposed LAZERS dispatch operation; every path fails before creating a child and child-session count remains unchanged. Legitimate editing/shell/Code Mode operations still work under otherwise allowing host policy. Denial is mechanically enforced on known host/tool dispatch paths, not prompt-only advice or hiding tool descriptions. This does not claim an operating-system sandbox for arbitrary shell commands, and no general scheduler/worker dispatch is introduced by the test harness.

Context assembly tests include repository rules, exact task/spec refs, relevant source/test evidence and selected-skill source/version refs supplied by an authorized policy context, without duplicate instructions on reuse. Requested-but-unresolved, denied/missing skill, changed skill/source, oversized mandatory material and unconfirmed delivery remain explicitly incomplete/prerequisite, never successful delivered/admitted status. Model/skill selections are not silently changed by context tooling; unset default and explicit authorized selection provenance are retained, with no paid fallback. Packet tests distinguish source retrieval from host skill attachment/delivery and document the runner-owned delivery/admission boundary, including future resumed/compacted paths.

The spike/handoff and shared-tool contracts link both investigation specifications and explicitly state this clarified role/context boundary; the original task is not silently revised or duplicated. Scope review confirms no durable runner, dispatch/state/budget/verification/acceptance engine or GUI changes, no stored task started, and runner task record is untouched. Existing specialist and task receipt/retained-callback tests pass, shared-path edits preserve concurrent work, and original index budgets/security remain enforced for the new implementor consumer. Actual initial/final source hashes identify the integrated artifact rather than attributing working-tree source to initial HEAD.

Bun behavior tests and native formatter/linter/typechecker pass against the named artifact. The record includes effective role-policy matrix, ContextPacket contribution/delivery boundary, exact native tools and model/skill provenance, real context/delegation-denial traces, test outputs, measured or unavailable usage, linked task IDs and unresolved operational gates. Do not claim runner enforcement or acceptance from context retrieval, mocked role config, a persisted receipt or unperformed native checks.
